Chapter 9. The Power and Price of Belief.
You know, belief really is a double-edged sword. On one hand, it lifts us up—spurring people toward greatness, giving them the courage to take on impossible odds, or even helping them find meaning in the middle of chaos.
But there’s another side to it, too. Sometimes, belief can blind us. It can make us ignore uncomfortable truths or hold on to comfortable lies, even when deep down, we know better.
Take Superman, for example. As he soared from comic book pages to become a global icon, the beliefs wrapped up in his story only grew stronger—and honestly, more tangled. Fans clung to the hope that justice would always win, truly believing in the hero’s goodness. Corporations, on the other hand, saw the brand’s power—believing in profits and the magic of a symbol that brought hope to millions.
And then there were the creators. At first, they believed their work could change the world. In so many ways—it really did. But that belief came with a hefty price tag.
The men who dreamed up Superman ended up fighting just to be recognized, struggling for a share of the success their creation brought to everyone else. Lawsuits dragged on for years. Friendships that once seemed unbreakable were put to the test. Suddenly, the line between hero and victim wasn’t so clear anymore. The world might’ve wanted a simple, uplifting story—but the truth? It was a lot more complicated.
And it’s not just in comic books. Think about your own life for a second. In those quiet moments, we all wrestle with our own beliefs. Maybe it’s a parent who believes their child will be safe, even when the world feels uncertain. Or a worker who trusts that their hard work will eventually be noticed, even if recognition takes its sweet time.
Most of us don’t even realize just how much our lives are shaped by what we choose to believe—and how tough it can be to let go of a belief when it’s no longer helping us.
So, here’s the real takeaway: belief is both a gift and a burden. It can lift us up, sure. But sometimes, it can hold us back, too. The hard part is figuring out when to hold on tight—and when it’s time to finally let go.
